subject: English Language
text: If she ____ earlier, she would have caught the bus.
explanation: Third conditional requires past perfect in the if-clause: 'If she had left' for an unreal past condition.

subject: English Language
text: Neither the manager nor the assistants ____ willing to sign the document.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject; 'assistants' is plural so use 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: Tom said, 'I will finish by noon.' → Tom said that he ____ finish by noon.
explanation: In reported speech backshift changes 'will' to 'would'; use 'would' to indicate future-in-the-past.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best synonym for 'abundant' in: 'The harvest was abundant this year.'
explanation: 'Abundant' means plentiful or in large quantity; 'scarce', 'meagre' and 'barren' are opposites.

subject: English Language
text: The committee accepted the apology and the matter was finally ____.
explanation: 'Put to rest' means to settle or resolve an issue; 'swept under the carpet' implies hiding rather than resolving.

subject: English Language
text: Which version is correctly capitalised for this sentence: 'the governor of oyo state will arrive tomorrow.'
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
The Governor of Oyo State will arrive tomorrow.
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Official titles and proper nouns take capitals: 'Governor' (as title) and 'Oyo State' (proper name) must be capitalised.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable has the primary stress in the word 'photograph'?
explanation: 'Photograph' carries primary stress on the first syllable (PHO-to-graph); compare 'photography' which shifts stress.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the most appropriate response to: 'My flight got delayed; I’ll be late.'
options: That's unfortunate — do you want me to wait?
explanation: Responding with empathy and offering help is an appropriate speech act; the other options are irrelevant or dismissive.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: 'They will publish the report next week.'
options: The report will be published next week.
Next week the report will have been published by them.
The report will publish next week.
Next week the report is publishing.
explanation: Passive uses the object as subject plus 'will' + past participle: 'The report will be published next week.'

subject: English Language
text: Maya rescued an injured pigeon and nursed it back to health. When she finally released it, she felt ____.
explanation: Context shows successful rescue and release, so a positive feeling like 'triumphant' fits; others contradict the success described.

subject: English Language
text: Each of the students ____ a laptop for the exam.
explanation: Rule: 'Each' is singular and takes a singular verb; therefore use 'has' not 'have' or plural forms.

subject: English Language
text: If Musa ____ the map, we would not have gotten lost.
explanation: Third conditional requires past perfect in the if-clause ('had read') with a modal perfect in the main clause to show unreal past.

subject: English Language
text: By the end of the year, the choir ____ together for five years.
explanation: Duration up to a future point uses the future perfect continuous: 'will have been singing' shows continuous action for five years.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best synonym for 'dwindle' in: 'The crowd began to dwindle after midnight.'
explanation: 'Dwindle' means to become smaller or fewer; 'shrink' correctly matches decrease. 'Flourish' and 'increase' are opposites.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the most appropriate response to: 'Congratulations on your promotion!'
explanation: Polite acknowledgement of congratulations uses a grateful response such as 'Thanks a million'; other options are irrelevant or rude.

subject: English Language
text: Which version is correctly capitalised for this sentence: 'she will attend the university of ghana in september.'
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
She will attend the University of Ghana in September.
explanation: Proper nouns and months are capitalised: 'University of Ghana' and 'September' require capitals; correct punctuation and case in option 1.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable has the primary stress in the word 'biography'?
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
explanation: Pronunciation: 'biography' is /baɪˈɒɡrəfi/ with primary stress on the second syllable ('bi-O-gra-phy').

subject: English Language
text: Choose the most appropriate reply to: 'Could you lend me Naira 200 for the bus?'
options: I suppose the weather is fine.
Yes, I will lend you Naira 200 right now.
explanation: Polite agreement to a direct request is a clear offer like 'Yes, I will lend you Naira 200 right now.' Other replies do not answer the request.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: 'Someone stole the teacher's laptop yesterday.'
options: Someone was stolen the teacher's laptop yesterday.
The teacher's laptop stolen yesterday by someone.
The teacher's laptop was stolen yesterday.
Yesterday the teacher's laptop has been stolen.
explanation: Passive of simple past: object becomes subject and uses past simple passive 'was stolen'. Other options are ungrammatical or wrong tense.

subject: English Language
text: Complete the sentence: She insisted ____ paying for the broken window.
explanation: Verb pattern: 'insist' is followed by the preposition 'on' plus a gerund ('insisted on paying'); other prepositions are incorrect.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct verb to complete: "A bunch of bananas ____ ready to sell."
explanation: Collective noun 'a bunch' is treated as a single unit; use singular verb 'is'. This contrasts with plural verbs used when the focus is on individual items.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best completion: "By this time next year, I ____ the course."
explanation: The future perfect ('will have' + past participle) expresses an action completed before a specified future time: 'will have completed' is required here.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best synonym for 'meticulous' in: "He checked the figures with meticulous care."
explanation: 'Meticulous' means very careful and precise; 'thorough' matches this meaning. The other options are antonyms or unrelated.

subject: English Language
text: What does 'bite the bullet' mean in: "After months of delay, the team decided to bite the bullet and start the project."
explanation: The idiom 'bite the bullet' means to accept and endure an unpleasant but necessary action; it does not mean to delay or celebrate.

subject: English Language
text: Insert comma(s) correctly into this sentence: "While cooking the children played in the yard"
options: While cooking, the children played in the yard.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: An introductory subordinate clause ('While cooking') should be followed by a comma before the main clause: 'While cooking, the children...' is correct punctuation.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable has the primary stress in the word 'banana'?
explanation: The word 'banana' has primary stress on the second syllable: ba-NA-na. Stress pattern affects pronunciation and distinguishes syllable prominence.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: 'coat', 'goat', 'boat', 'cough'?
explanation: 'Coat', 'goat' and 'boat' share the long vowel /oʊ/ (in many accents). 'Cough' has a different vowel and consonant ending (/ɒf/ or /ɔf/), so it differs.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the most appropriate response to: "I failed my driving test today."
options: Can you lend me your car?
Why did you take the test?
I'm sorry to hear that; you'll do better next time.
explanation: An appropriate supportive response expresses sympathy and encouragement. Option 2 shows empathy and reassurance, unlike the other less relevant replies.

subject: English Language
text: Transform to passive: "The chef prepared the feast for the guests."
options: The feast was prepared for the guests by the chef.
The guests were prepared the feast by the chef.
The chef was prepared the feast for the guests.
Preparations of the feast were made by the guests.
explanation: In passive voice the object ('the feast') becomes subject and the verb uses 'was prepared' + agent 'by the chef': 'The feast was prepared for the guests by the chef.'

subject: English Language
text: Amina left her umbrella on the bus, and yet she arrived dry. What is the most plausible explanation?
options: The bus had a roof and windows
It did not rain during her journey
She sat under a shelter all the time
The umbrella was heavier than her bag
explanation: If she left her umbrella but arrived dry, the simplest inference is that it did not rain during the journey. This is a direct and economical explanation compared with the others.

subject: English Language
text: Either the headteacher or the students ____ responsible for decorating the hall.
explanation: With subjects joined by 'either...or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject; 'students' is plural so use 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By the time we reached the station, the train ____ away.
explanation: Use past perfect ('had left') for an action completed before another past action; simple past 'left' is incorrect here.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best synonym for 'sparse' in: 'The farmland had sparse crops this season.'
explanation: 'Sparse' means few or thinly spread; 'scanty' matches this meaning, unlike 'abundant' or 'plentiful'.

subject: English Language
text: What does the idiom mean in: 'Before we spend more money, let's run it up the flagpole.'
explanation: 'Run it up the flagpole' is an idiom meaning to test or float an idea informally to see reactions.

subject: English Language
text: Which version is correctly capitalised for this sentence: 'last week, governor adeola visited the federal hospital.'
options: The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
Last week, Governor Adeola visited the Federal Hospital.
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Capitals: beginning of sentence + titles and proper nouns ('Governor Adeola') and institutions as proper nouns ('Federal Hospital').

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable has the primary stress in the word 'community' ?
explanation: 'Community' is pronounced /kəˈmjuːnɪti/ with primary stress on the second syllable (mjuː).

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: 'cat', 'can', 'car', 'cap' ?
explanation: 'Car' has a different vowel (/ɑː/ or /a/) while 'cat', 'can', 'cap' share the short /æ/ vowel sound.

subject: English Language
text: Change to passive: 'The committee will announce the winners tomorrow.'
options: Tomorrow, will the winners be announced by the committee?
The winners will be announced by the committee tomorrow.
The winners will announce by the committee tomorrow.
The winners are being announced by the committee tomorrow.
explanation: Passive: object becomes subject + 'will be' + past participle: 'The winners will be announced by the committee tomorrow.'

subject: English Language
text: When the fire alarm sounded, everyone ____ to the nearest exit.
explanation: Sequence of past events uses simple past for completed actions: 'sounded' and then 'rushed' (past simple) is correct.

subject: English Language
text: Amina put a note marked 'Confidential' on a stack of documents and left the room. Why did she write 'Confidential' on the note?
options: to invite people to read them
to show they were old papers
to indicate secrecy and restrict access
explanation: 'Confidential' signals secrecy and restricted access; it does not indicate age, weight, or invitation to read.

subject: English Language
text: Neither the laptop nor the chargers ____ missing from the office.
explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer noun; 'chargers' is plural so use 'are'.

subject: English Language
text: By the time he arrived, they _____ dinner.
explanation: Use past perfect ('had finished') to show an action completed before another past event ('he arrived').

subject: English Language
text: Choose the best synonym for 'frugal' in: 'She lives a frugal life to save for university.'
explanation: 'Frugal' means economical or 'thrifty'; the other choices contrast with careful saving (extravagant, careless, generous).

subject: English Language
text: What does 'call the shots' mean in: 'As team captain, Bola calls the shots during training.'
explanation: The idiom 'call the shots' means to make decisions or give orders; other options are unrelated roles.

subject: English Language
text: Which version is correctly capitalised for this sentence: "next monday, dr. lara adamu will speak at the auditorium."
options: Next Monday, Dr. Lara Adamu will speak at the auditorium.
The stated rule does not apply in this context
A different grammatical construction is required
The sentence has no acceptable completion here
explanation: Capitals required for the day, title and each name: 'Next Monday, Dr. Lara Adamu...'. 'Auditorium' is a common noun and need not be capitalised here.

subject: English Language
text: Which syllable has the primary stress in the word 'economics'?
explanation: The primary stress in 'economics' falls on the third syllable (e-co-NOM-ics): phonetic pattern /ˌiːkəˈnɒmɪks/.

subject: English Language
text: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others: 'clear', 'dear', 'here', 'heart'?
explanation: 'Clear', 'dear' and 'here' share a similar vowel (diphthong /ɪə/ or /ɪr/), while 'heart' uses a different vowel (/ɑː/), so 'heart' is different.

subject: English Language
text: Choose the correct passive form of: 'They have completed the bridge.'
explanation: Present perfect passive is formed with 'has/have been' + past participle. For singular 'bridge' use 'has been completed'.

subject: English Language
text: She would rather ____ at home than go out.
explanation: After 'would rather' use the base form of the verb without 'to' or -s; correct: 'would rather stay'.

subject: English Language
text: Ola returned the library book a week late and refused the fine, pointing to a torn page. What is the most plausible reason for her refusal?
options: The book was already torn before she borrowed it.
She had lost the book earlier.
She had already paid the fine online.
explanation: Ola's pointing to a torn page implies she claims the damage existed before her loan; therefore she refuses responsibility for the fine.
